title: Morehead State football prepares to host Drake after Homecoming win
text:
Sports
Morehead State football prepares to host Drake after Homecoming win
Morehead State football hosts Drake at Phil Simms Stadium following a Homecoming win over Stetson. The Eagles seek their first home victory over Drake since 2015 as both teams prepare for Saturday's matchup.
The Morehead State football team will host Drake at Phil Simms Stadium on Saturday, according to an Oct. 29 announcement. The game is scheduled for 1 p.m. Eastern Time and marks the team's second consecutive home game following a Homecoming victory.
Children in costume will receive free admission as part of Halloween festivities. Fans can listen to the broadcast on the Eagle Sports Radio Network, with WIVY-96.3 FM as the flagship station, or stream live coverage on ESPN+.
Morehead State seeks its first home win over Drake since a triple-overtime victory in 2015. The Eagles have a 4-12 all-time record against Drake but ended the Bulldogs' Pioneer Football League-best 17-game conference winning streak in their last meeting at Drake in 2024. Three of Morehead State's four wins against Drake have come at home.
Drake enters the matchup with a 2-6 overall record and leads the league in passing offense. For Morehead State, freshman running back Blake Fisher was named Pioneer League Freshman of the Week after totaling 128 yards and three touchdowns against Stetson last weekend. Quarterbacks Bryce Patterson and David Parsons have each thrown for exactly 982 yards through eight games this season, while wide receiver Anthony Ice ranks among national leaders with 654 receiving yards.
Defensively, Quinton Griffin has blocked both a punt and field goal this year, tying him for first nationally in blocked kicks among Football Championship Subdivision players. Safety Sidney Webb is third in total tackles within the conference and has recorded double-digit tackles multiple times this season.
Kicker Jordan Price remains perfect on point-after-touchdown attempts for his career, having converted all 55 tries so far—reportedly making him the first Eagle kicker to achieve more than fifty consecutive successful PATs.
